info.name: SAP AI Application Lab (v0.1.0)
info.description:
Generated by scripts/generate_api_collection.py - do not edit by hand.

Set the `baseUrl` variable to point at your API (default http://127.0.0.1:8000). Every response uses the shared envelope {success, data, error, meta}; downloads return the file itself.

Demo application: not connected to any SAP system, and no output has been validated in a live SAP environment.

variable.description: Unused today - no endpoint requires a credential. Present so the Authorization header is already wired when authentication is added.

item.name: System
item.description: Health, the module index and the OpenAPI document. `GET /api/v1/health` reports the database and the resolved AI provider and needs no credential - it is what a container healthcheck polls.

request.description: Report application, database and AI provider status.

Return an index of the available modules and where to start.

The first call a new client makes. It answers "what is here", "where do I
read the contract" and "am I allowed to believe these numbers", which is
everything needed before the second call.

item.name: Purchase Order Risk Checker
item.description: **Module 1.** Upload an SAP-style purchase order export and get findings from 20 deterministic rules: duplicates, split orders, price anomalies, missing approvals, contract gaps, late deliveries and data quality problems. Every finding carries its rule, its evidence, a severity and an estimated exposure. Upload → analyse → read findings → download the report.

request.description: Validate a purchase order file, store it and suggest a column mapping.
Run every enabled deterministic rule against a previously uploaded file.
Return previous analyses, newest first.
Return KPIs, supplier risk, data quality issues and the AI narrative.
Return a filtered, paginated list of findings.

Download the analysis as XLSX, CSV or JSON.

This route returns the file itself rather than the JSON envelope, so a
browser or ``fetch`` call can stream it straight to a download.
Return every configured rule with its thresholds.
Return the canonical fields and the SAP column names that map to them.
Download the bundled fictional sample purchase order file.
Describe the bundled demo dataset, including its anomaly manifest size.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.

item.name: Spend Analytics Dashboard
item.description: **Module 2.** Turn a procurement transaction export into the figures a category manager asks for: spend under management, maverick spend, contract leakage, supplier concentration, price variance and modelled savings. Every opportunity is labelled an estimate and states the assumption behind it. The drill-down endpoint returns exactly the transactions behind any chart element.

request.description: Validate a spend file, store it and suggest a column mapping.
Calculate metrics, breakdowns and savings opportunities for an upload.
Return previous spend analyses, newest first.
Return metrics, analytics breakdowns, opportunities and the narrative.

query.description: One of: category, company_code, currency, material, material_group, plant, purchasing_group, purchasing_org, spend_month, subcategory, supplier

request.description:
Return the transactions behind a summary figure.

Send the ``dimension`` and ``value`` of the chart element the user clicked
to get exactly the lines that produced it.

Return modelled savings opportunities.

Every figure returned here is an estimate produced from the uploaded data
under the documented assumptions, not a guaranteed saving.
Download the analysis as XLSX, CSV or JSON.
Return the canonical fields and the column names that map to them.
Return every savings rule with the assumptions it applies.
Describe how every figure is calculated, including the disclaimers.
Download the bundled fictional spend transaction file.
Describe the bundled demo dataset and its scenario manifest.

item.name: Supplier Recommendation Engine
item.description: **Module 3.** Rank the suppliers that can meet a requirement, using nine normalised scores and configurable weights. Eligibility is applied *before* ranking, and a supplier that was excluded says why.

request.description: Validate a supplier file, store it and load it into a catalogue.
Return the canonical supplier fields and the column names that map to them.
Return every uploaded supplier catalogue, newest first.
Download the bundled fictional supplier master file.
Describe the bundled demo supplier catalogue and its manifest.
Return suppliers from a catalogue (the most recent one by default).
Return one supplier from a catalogue (the most recent one by default).
Apply eligibility filters, score every eligible supplier and rank them.
Return previous recommendations, newest first.
Return the documented scoring model: weights, formulas and eligibility filters.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.
Return the ranked suppliers, scores, advantages, risks and narrative.
Download the recommendation as XLSX, CSV or JSON.

item.name: Invoice Validator
item.description: **Module 4.** Three-way match invoices against purchase orders and goods receipts with configurable tolerances, and raise exceptions from 17 rules: quantity and price mismatches, duplicates, overbilling, date problems and missing documents. Upload the three datasets, then validate.

request.description: Validate a file, store it and suggest a column mapping for the dataset.
Three-way match the uploaded invoices and raise deterministic exceptions.
Return previous validations, newest first.
Return KPIs, supplier summary, three-way-match rows and the AI narrative.
Return a filtered, paginated list of exceptions.
Download the validation as XLSX, CSV or JSON.
Return the canonical fields for all three datasets and their SAP aliases.
Return every configured rule with the active tolerances and policies.
Download one of the bundled fictional demo files.
Describe the bundled demo invoice datasets and their scenario manifest.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.

item.name: Supplier Risk Copilot
item.description: **Module 5.** Score a supplier portfolio across ten risk categories with a transparent weighted model, then ask questions answered *from the loaded records* with citations. A question the data cannot answer is refused and says why, rather than being guessed.

item.name: Upload supplier risk profiles or risk events

request.description:
Validate a supplier risk file, store it and load it.

``profiles`` starts a new dataset; ``events`` attaches the dated internal
records that drive the risk trend and the copilot's citations.
Return every uploaded supplier risk dataset, newest first.
Return the canonical risk fields and the column names that map to them.

item.name: Download the demo supplier risk dataset

request.description: Download a bundled fictional supplier risk file.
Describe the bundled demo supplier risk dataset and its manifest.
Return the categories, weights, metrics, bands and missing-data behaviour.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.
Score every supplier in a dataset across the ten risk categories.
Return previous risk assessments, newest first.

Answer a question about the loaded supplier risk data, with citations.

The answer is produced by deterministic rules over the computed assessment.
When the information is not in the loaded records, the copilot says so.
Return assessed suppliers, highest risk first.

Return the full risk profile: category breakdown, trend, supporting
records and recommended actions.
Return one assessment with its ranked suppliers.

item.name: Contract Assistant
item.description: **Module 6.** Extract clauses, key dates, obligations and risks from a text-based PDF, DOCX or TXT contract. Every claim carries a page number, a section heading, an excerpt and a deterministic confidence score. A scanned document is reported as needing OCR rather than analysed as an empty contract. Uploaded documents are treated strictly as data.

request.description:
Validate a contract document, store it and extract its text.

Text-based PDF, DOCX and TXT work with no OCR provider. A scanned document
is accepted, reported as ``needs_ocr`` and explained - never silently
analysed as an empty contract.

Extract clauses, dates, obligations and risks from a stored contract.

Every result is produced by deterministic rules. The optional AI narrative
only explains them and lands in its own fields.
Return uploaded contracts, newest first.
Return the clause types, the risk rules and the confidence formula.

Report which document types can be read, and whether OCR is configured.

Credentials are never included - only whether each provider is installed
and configured.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.
Download one bundled fictional contract.
Describe the bundled fictional contracts and their manifest.
Return the contract with its clauses, dates, obligations and risks.
Return the extracted clauses, each with page, heading, excerpt and confidence.

item.name: Ask a question about a contract

request.description:
Answer a question from the extracted clauses, citing page and heading.

The answer is produced deterministically from what was extracted. When the
contract does not cover the question, the assistant says so rather than
producing a plausible sentence.
Download the analysis as XLSX, CSV or JSON.

item.name: Inventory Predictor
item.description: **Module 7.** Forecast demand per material and plant with five explainable statistical models chosen by backtesting, project stock forward over real calendar days, and get shortage dates, reorder plans and stock classifications. No AI produces any number here.

request.description:
Validate an inventory history file, store it and load it into a dataset.

The response describes every material/plant series the file contains, the
period granularity that was inferred from the dates, and any data-quality
problems found while loading.
Return every uploaded inventory dataset, newest first.
Return the canonical inventory fields and the column names that map to them.

item.name: The documented forecasting and planning method

request.description:
Return every forecasting method with its assumptions, plus the model
selection rules, the reorder policy formulae and the stock thresholds.
Download the bundled fictional inventory history.
Describe the bundled demo inventory dataset and its scenario manifest.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.

Forecast every material in a dataset and project its stock forward.

For each material/plant the engine backtests the eligible statistical models,
picks the winner, forecasts the horizon with a confidence range, projects the
stock day by day, and derives the shortage date, the reorder date and
quantity, the recommended safety stock and the stock classification.
Return previous forecast runs, newest first.
Return the run's settings, portfolio summary, data-quality issues and materials.

item.name: List materials in a forecast run

request.description: Return a filtered, paginated list of materials, soonest shortage first.

Return the full result for one material: history, forecast with its
confidence range, every model candidate and its backtest score, the projected
stock path, the reorder rationale and the data-quality warnings.
Download the forecast run as XLSX, CSV or JSON.

item.name: SAP Test Case Generator
item.description: **Module 8.** Describe an SAP business process and get an editable test suite across eight test types. The identifiers, the type coverage, the priorities and the step numbering are decided by code before a provider is contacted; only the wording is drafted. Edit, approve, record execution results, export.

item.name: Generate a suite of SAP test cases

request.description:
Generate a test suite from a business process description.

The identifiers, the type allocation and the priorities are computed by
deterministic Python before any provider is called. If the provider is
unavailable, or ``use_ai`` is false, the configured templates fill every
case - the suite is complete either way, and each case says which produced
it.

item.name: Test types, limits and the deterministic rules

request.description: Return the supported test types and how the generator makes its decisions.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.
Describe the bundled fictional SAP process definitions.
Return one fictional process definition, ready to post to ``/generate``.
Return generated suites, newest first.

item.name: Get one suite with its test cases

request.description: Return the suite, its coverage, its summary and every test case.

item.name: Add a test case to a suite

request.description: Add one test case by hand. It receives the next free identifier of its type.
Download the suite as XLSX, CSV, JSON or PDF.
Return one test case by its id, or by its identifier when that is unique.

Apply a partial edit. Only the fields present in the body are changed.

Editing the script (type, title, objective, preconditions, test data, steps
or expected result) clears any approval and returns the case to draft, just
as regenerating does - the approval described the script that was replaced.
Editing only the administrative fields leaves the approval in place.
Delete one test case and report the coverage the suite lost.

Redraft the script of one test case, keeping its place in the suite.

The approval is cleared, because it belonged to the script that was
replaced. The execution record is kept unless the request says otherwise.
Copy a test case's script into a new row with its own identifier.

item.name: Approve or un-approve one test case

request.description: Record a review decision against one test case.
Record what happened when the test was run. The script is never changed.

item.name: SAP Blueprint Generator
item.description: **Module 9.** Describe an SAP implementation project and get a thirty-section blueprint you can edit, approve, version and compare. Sections computed from the project request cannot be invented by a model, and a section with no input says so instead of being filled in.

request.description:
Generate a complete blueprint from a structured project request.

The section list, the section order, the organisational structure, the
module list, the integration register, the interface list, the migration
sources and the security roles are computed by deterministic Python before
any provider is called. If the provider is unavailable, or ``use_ai`` is
false, the configured templates write every section - the document is
complete either way, and each section says which produced it.

A section whose required project fields are empty is returned as
``needs_input`` with the missing field named, never filled with invention.

The result is a **proposed** blueprint requiring review by qualified SAP
professionals. No configuration described in it has been validated against a
live SAP system.

item.name: Sections, project fields and the deterministic rules

request.description: Return the supported sections and how the generator makes its decisions.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.
Describe the bundled fictional SAP project definitions.
Return one fictional project definition, ready to post to ``/generate``.
Return generated blueprints, newest first.

item.name: Get one blueprint with its sections

request.description: Return the blueprint, its summary and every section.

Apply a partial edit to the blueprint's own fields.

Sending ``project`` replaces the project request, which is how a section
waiting for an input gets unblocked. The sections whose items are computed
from the request are rebuilt from the new values and their approvals are
cleared - a blueprint whose organisational structure disagrees with its own
project request would be worse than one that is out of date.

Download the blueprint as Markdown, JSON, DOCX or PDF.

Every format carries the disclaimer, the provenance of each section and the
sections that are still waiting for project input.
Add one custom section, optionally positioned after an existing one.
Return one section by its identifier (``BP-SCOPE``), its key (``scope``) or its id.

Apply a partial edit. Only the fields present in the body are changed.

Editing the content (title, narrative or items) clears any approval and
returns the section to draft, just as regenerating does - the approval
described the words that were replaced. Editing only the status or the
comments leaves the approval in place.
Delete one custom section. The standard sections cannot be deleted.

Redraft one section's wording, keeping its place in the document.

The approval is cleared, because it belonged to the wording that was
replaced. The section's factual items are recomputed from the project
request, never redrafted.
Record a review decision against one section.
Return the version history, newest first.

item.name: Save the current state as a version

request.description: Freeze the blueprint's current sections as an immutable version.

Compare two saved versions, section by section.

Version ``0`` means "the blueprint as it stands now", so
``?from=2&to=0`` answers the question a reviewer asks most often: what have
I changed since I last saved?

Return one saved version with its full section snapshot.

Version ``0`` returns the live document in the same shape, without saving it.

item.name: SAP Interview Coach
item.description: **Module 10.** Practise SAP interview questions and get a scored, explained result. The rubric marks the answer; a provider is only ever asked for the prose around a finished verdict, so the same answer scores the same with a real model, with the mock, or with no AI at all. An answer key never travels with an unanswered question.

request.description:
Start an interview and serve the first question.

The question list is drawn from the bundled bank by a seeded, deterministic
selection: the same tracks, mode, difficulties and seed always produce the
same interview. The questions come back **without** their marking schemes;
each answer key is attached to the answer once it has been submitted.

Return average score, breakdowns, trends, weak areas and the study plan.

Every figure is calculated from the recorded answers by deterministic
Python, including the study plan: the topics it names are the ones with the
lowest recorded averages and the concepts it names are the ones those
answers actually missed.

item.name: Tracks, modes, bands and the marking rules

request.description: Return the tracks, modes, difficulties, bands and the published rubric.

List questions from the bundled bank.

Answer keys are never included, whatever the filters say: this endpoint
exists so a candidate can see what a track covers, not so they can revise
the marking scheme.
Describe the bundled, entirely fictional question bank.
Report which AI provider is active. API keys are never included.
Return interview sessions, newest first.
Return the session with every question asked, answer given and score.

item.name: Submit an answer and get the feedback

request.description:
Mark one answer against its rubric and serve the next question.

Every number in the response - the overall score, each dimension, the band,
the pass verdict - is produced by deterministic Python from the question's
rubric. ``use_ai`` decides only who writes the coaching prose; the scores are
identical with a provider, with the mock and with ``use_ai=false``.

Close the session and return it with its final summary.

Completing with questions unanswered is allowed and reported: the summary
carries ``pending_count`` and every average is over what was answered.
